input.quote: Kubient hereby grants to Customer a limited, royalty-free, non-exclusive, non-transferable, non-assignable, without right of sublicense, revocable license to access, participate in and use to the full extent the Auction Platform as hosted by Kubient, for the purpose of serving Inventory at Target Demand
input.rationale: The only grant of rights to us (paragraph 2, Auction Platform licence) runs solely to "Customer" as defined in the preamble (The Associated Press alone, with no affiliate coverage and no defined "Affiliate"), and is expressly "non-transferable, non-assignable", so it fails both fallback elements: affiliates have no path to coverage and the licence cannot follow us into a merger or acquisition (the assignment proviso in paragraph 14(h) covers the Agreement generally, not this restricted licence). We therefore drafted at fallback: affiliates covered on written notice and transfer to an M&A successor. We deliberately did not target preferred: the licence is royalty-free and coterminous with the Services, and making it perpetual/irrevocable or terminable only for uncured material breach would require collateral rewrites of the termination mechanic in paragraph 4(c)(ii) ("the license granted under section 3 shall be revoked"). The retained "revocable" wording and the absence of contractor coverage remain short of our preferred position and are noted rather than redlined at this level.

mappings.element: Customer's affiliates are covered on written notice.
The licence is transferable to a successor in a merger or acquisition transaction.

proposal.summary: Extend Auction Platform licence to Customer affiliates on written notice and permit transfer to an M&A successor
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We extended the Auction Platform licence to Customer's affiliates upon written notice and made it transferable to a successor by merger or acquisition, which is our fallback licence-scope position.
